summary: Two sampled material sheets exchange places through exact prescribed affine paths. The local formulas, area preservation and native CPU encoding are checked; browser rendering and touch interaction remain unverified. This is not a fluid solver or a verification of the manuscript’s broader claims.

claims.claim: Four partial shears preserve planar area and finish at reciprocal stretch.
claims.how: The chronological maps are Y(-λ), X(1/λ-1), Y(1), X(λ-1), each evaluated from the original material label. Enabled λ values are 0.5, 1 and 2. Each partial derivative has determinant one.

sources.title: Finite Instructions and Solenoidal Shear Flows, §3, Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, pp. 5–9
sources.says: Four chronological shears produce reciprocal scaling; seven separated smooth pulses realize lifted affine paths.

claims.note: The λ=1 endpoint is identity in the plane but its intermediate shear detour remains nonconstant.

claims.claim: The seven stages use smooth separated time pulses.
claims.how: Stage j uses S(16t-(2j-1)), where S is the exponential flat-step function. Each active interval is followed by a resting gap; the endpoint never wraps to the start.

claims.claim: Both marked material patches retain area 0.04.
claims.how: Eight extra native tokens carry the exact corners of two 0.2-by-0.2 material squares. Their edge outlines use two-token interpolation. Tests use signed polygon area, not bounding-box or pixel area.

claims.claim: The compact scene satisfies the stated separation and excursion bounds.
claims.how: Source centers are (-1.25,0) and (1.25,0), targets exchange centers, source half-width is 0.4, private heights are 1.25 and 2.5, and h=1. Worst target gap is 0.9; all shear offsets stay within 1.2.

claims.claim: Native encoded particle centers represent the affine material paths.
claims.how: Each sheet uses four corner tokens. Original labels use the same 10-bit u,v weights as native skin4. Tests decode the native buffer and float32 token offsets after fit, with construction-coordinate tolerance 0.00002.

claims.claim: Pinning chooses an actual material sample and shows its complete seven-segment path.
claims.how: Inverse current affine maps identify candidate sheets; the nearest existing quantized sample is selected. Native two-token segments connect eight exact stage nodes. Replay resets original labels.

simplified: Only two material sheets and one bounded seven-stage instruction are shown.
The global divergence-free velocity, compensating lobes, forcing, pressure, energy and viscosity are not evaluated.
Particle size, opacity, color, covariance and sound are styling; projected density and pixel area are not conserved physical quantities.
The complete pinned path includes future positions. Replaying resets; scrubbing backward retraces the same prescribed path.
No computation, halting, global theorem audit or Lean verification is claimed.
